  INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE’S MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION OF SOAH
          ORDER 24 DISMISSING 839 INTERVENORS EN MASSE

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

  I.​   INTRODUCTION
    A.​ George Noelke (“Noelke”), Intervenor in 59182 and 59475 here provides his MOTION FOR
        CLARIFICATION to the Honorable ALJ’s ruling in SOAH ORDER 24.
    B.​ The pleading and responses at issue in this clarification request are:
            1.​ Noelke’s Objection to Applicants’ List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or
                Statement of Position And His Motion to Provide Notice and Opportunity For Hearing
                Before Intervenor Dismissal En Masse, Item 4706.
            2.​ Applicants’ Response to Noelke’s Objection to Applicants List of Intervenors Who Did
                Not File Testimony or Statement of Position, Item 4932.
            3.​ Noelke’s Response to Applicants’ Response Regarding Dismissal of More than 800
                Intervenors En Masse, Item 5105.
    C.​ In response to the above pleading and responses, the Honorable ALJs’ ruling briefly restated
        Noelke’s and the Appplicants’ arguments and then stated only, “Having considered the pleadings,
        Mr. Noelke’s Objection is OVERRULED and his motion is DENIED.”




                                                                                                       1
     D.​ At pages 9-17 of Order 24, the ALJs dismiss exactly 839 Intervenors for failing to file either a
        Statement of Position or direct testimony. (Noelke was not in that group for reasons stated in his
        pleading and response.)
 II.​   LEGAL ARGUMENT
    A.​ The Texas APA at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051(2) provides that Noelke, an Intervenor and
        thereby a “party” to this contested case, is “entitled to an opportunity…to respond and to present
        evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.” Emphasis added.
    B.​ Noelke asserts that each of the 839 Intervenors dismissed in Order 24 are similarly entitled under
        § 2001.051(2). A notice of default has not been served on them, and so they remain “parties” in
        this contested case.
    C.​ Noelke respectfully observes that the ALJs’ ruling “Having considered the pleadings, Mr.
        Noelke’s Objection is OVERRULED and his motion is DENIED.” is ambiguous and fails to state
        a reasoned basis. He cannot ascertain whether his objection and motion were overruled and
        denied on procedural grounds, jurisdictional grounds, on the substantive merits or any other
        reasoned basis. The ruling failed to state any findings or conclusions, and it is without any legal
        reasoning. The ruling thereby makes it impossible for Noelke and the 839 dismissed Intervenors
        to respond to and argue the issue(s), as allowed in 2001.051(2), identified by the ALJs because no
        issue was identified by them in the ruling.
    D.​ The ambiguity of Order 24 has created a review defect in violation of due course of law and due
        process provisions of the Texas and U.S. Constitutions. Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I, §
        19, the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1. This ambiguity prevents Noelke and the
        dismissed Intervenors from raising any specific issue on appeal to either the PUC Commissioners
        or to a Travis County District Court under the Texas APA at § 2001.174.

III. CLARIFICATION REQUESTED ​
Noelke respectfully requests that the ALJs authoring Order 24 identify their reasoned basis for denying
his objection and motion. Noelke also requests other and further relief to which he may be entitled.

Signed June 2, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
/s/ George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se landowner
